entry: Target VM p15-dev-2604 created by a VBoxManage script (create-p15-vm.ps1): 4 vCPU, 8 GB, 64 GB fixed VDI, EFI, NAT ssh 2222->22. First attempt via GUI wizard produced a 25 GB disk with LVM (11 GB root) and was discarded.
Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic; linux-generic/-image/-headers held; unattended-upgrades disabled; no HWE kernel package; root on plain ext4; 4 GB swap file present.
LSM list has no bpf (lockdown,capability,landlock,yama,apparmor,ima,evm); lockdown [none]; Secure Boot off; clocksource tsc; BTF present (7,067,009 B); timezone UTC.

clang 21.1.8, libbpf-dev 1.6.3, bpftool 7.7.0 built with its own libbpf 1.7 and an empty features line, pahole 1.31, bpftrace 0.25.0, Python 3.14.4. Two libbpf versions on one machine: vendor one pinned copy.

P1: all needed VFS, security_*, socket and io_uring functions present in BTF and ftrace; vfs_readv/vfs_writev hookable (no kprobe fallback needed); __sock_sendmsg absent (inlined) so fexit sock_sendmsg would miss callers; no .isra/.constprop clones; all 9 needed tracepoints present.
Live test: bpftrace fexit:vmlinux:vfs_read /retval > 0/ caught 769 reads, 795,645 bytes in 3 s. fexit attach + return value work on the target.

P2: tracing, raw_tracepoint, syscall, lsm program types; ringbuf, user_ringbuf, task_storage maps available; inode_storage NOT available (needs BPF-LSM). bpf_get_func_ret shows 0 program types: bpftool cannot probe tracing-only helpers; confirm with first real load.

P5 disk: direct 1 MiB seq write 63.7/105/92.3 MB/s; buffered 64 KiB + fdatasync per MiB 65.8/93.4/110 MB/s. Min ~64 MB/s => ~21 MB/s at 3x headroom => ~330k records/s at 64 B. Large variance under Hyper-V.

Rule broken: old 5.4 VM deleted before the new capture reproduced v3.7. v3.7 now comparable only through existing recordings (s1_mixed) + replay. Rule added: export a VM (VBoxManage export --ovf20, sha256) before deleting it.

Repo ranahunter10/fiery-dragon created (public, MIT + BPF dual). Empty root commit on main; governance merged as PR #1, but with a merge commit instead of squash. Next: repo settings to squash-only and a ruleset protecting main (maintainer applies in GitHub UI).
Phase-0 raw evidence (files 00-05) imported byte for byte into docs/evidence/phase0/ with SHA256SUMS; tarball sha256 334b1b2a...a6b223. This is now the evidence location for E-0001..E-0008.

Refines E-0007: in 03-p2-feature-probe.txt bpftool prints 'Could not determine which helpers are available' for tracing, struct_ops, ext and lsm program types, so absence of bpf_get_func_ret/bpf_d_path there says nothing about the kernel. Both remain to be shown by a real load (get_func_ret INF, d_path from fexit OPEN).

Maintainer decisions: (1) journals stay CSV in the repo; (2) vendor the latest libbpf 1.7.x tag, to match bpftool 7.7 which generates our skeletons (exact tag fixed in ADR-0002); (3) swap off only while measuring, recorded per run (ADR-0012); (4) Hyper-V stays on; a paired on/off experiment decides later (ADR-0012).

VM creation script committed as tools/vm/create-vm.ps1 (content identical to the file that built p15-dev-2604; original sha256 c8bbdb85...a55a91, only the final CRLF normalised to LF by .gitattributes) and runbook docs/runbooks/vm-setup.md with the 2026-10-21 lessons. Gap: the evidence-capture commands are not yet scripted.

Census probe (bench/census/census.bt) + summarizer: counts per record class with the design's own hooks, cumulative counters every 100 ms, log-budget verdict vs P5 (21.2 MB/s). Dry run in the dev container (tracepoints only, bpftrace 0.20.2): 30 prctl renames -> rename=30; exec=56 and rename_exec=56; 1000 loopback sends -> snd=1001.

task_rename fires on every exec (exec sets comm), so a naive rename count double-counts exec. Product rule: comm change at exec belongs in the EXEC record; RENAME records only for prctl/proc-comm/kthread renames. Found by the census dry run.

The cloud dev container (kernel 6.18.44, bpftrace 0.20.2) can attach BPF tracepoint programs (tracefs mountable, BTF present) but not fentry/fexit via bpftrace (available_filter_functions not readable). Usable for dry runs of tracepoint logic; VM stays authoritative.

VM smoke run: on Ubuntu 26.04, cat copies data with splice() through an internal pipe, not read()/write(): cat of a 100 MiB file plus seq|cat (588,895 B) gave do_splice = 210,892,990 B = 2 x (104,857,600 + 588,895), and only 0.8 MB of rd_reg. A read/write-only capture misses cat's data flow entirely; the do_splice hook is required, and an XFER record must name both ends (file->pipe, pipe->dest).
evidence: VM census smoke run 2026-10-25 (raw file to be committed as fixture)

entry: bpftrace 0.25 prints compiler warnings to stdout before the JSON stream (0.20 did not); delete() now returns a value and warns when discarded. Summarizer accepts non-JSON only before the start marker, counted and reported.

On kernel 7.0 the exec-rename classification failed: exec=68, rename_exec=2, rename=98 (=30 prctl + 68). On 6.18 (container) the same logic gave rename_exec=exec. Event order during exec on 7.0 under investigation (diagnostic sent).

Diagnostic on VM (kernel 7.0.0-38, bpftrace 0.25): for an exec of /bin/true, task_rename -> sched_process_exec -> syscalls:sys_exit_execve all fired, but syscalls:sys_enter_execve delivered nothing. On the dev container (kernel 6.18.44, bpftrace 0.20.2) all execve tracepoints fire (enter 25 / exit 26 / raw id=59 26). Cause (kernel vs bpftrace) OPEN. Census now brackets exec with raw_syscalls ids 59/322 instead. Product consequence: per-syscall tracepoints can go silent without error, so the self-test must cover every hook.

On kernel 7.0.0-38 with bpftrace 0.25, every syscalls:sys_enter_* tracepoint tested (execve, openat) delivers 0 events to BPF, while the same events appear in tracefs without BPF (sys_execve(filename: ... "/usr/bin/sudo" ...), now with user strings), and syscalls:sys_exit_* (26 execve, 240 openat) and raw_syscalls (26) deliver normally. Kernel-vs-bpftrace cause OPEN; deciding test is a plain libbpf tracepoint program in Phase 1. Consequence: a hook can attach without error and deliver nothing, so the load-time self-test is mandatory for every hook.

Census probe validated on the VM (kernel 7.0, bpftrace 0.25) with the raw_syscalls exec bracket: exec 68 / rename_exec 67, rename 31 (30 prctl + 1), splice exactly 210,892,990 B, dd 104,857,600 B written. 20 probes attached, output complete.

Census workload runner (bench/census/run.py) with six light workloads. Dry run in the dev container (8 s each, tracepoint-only probe): all ran and stopped cleanly; io-uring SKIPPED (no fio there); exec-storm rename_exec = exec = 5,611; file-churn ~118k ops of each kind in 8 s. 17 runner tests; 8/8 mutants killed.

First real census, light set, 60 s each, all ok, 0 lost (kernel 7.0, bpftrace 0.25, Hyper-V on). Emitted records/s mean/p99: idle 6/0, exec-storm 2,481/4,274, file-churn 38,320/79,951, super-producer 105,731/221,670 (max 353,461), xfer 261/2,236, io-uring 3,483/23,099. Only super-producer exceeds the 21.2 MB/s budget (28.4 MB/s p99 at assumed sizes).

Super-producer budget overrun comes from one class: OPEN = 99.91 % of emitted records (find opening directories; 221,434/s p99). At 64 B per open record p99 would be 14.2 MB/s (within). OPEN record size (path in every record vs once per file) and a directory-open kind decide the budget: inputs to ADR-0005/0006/0008.
io_uring file I/O bypasses vfs_read/vfs_write: fio steady state shows uring 2,454/s while rd_reg is 7/s. The io_uring hook is required.

cp on ext4: vfs_copy_file_range (60) falls back internally to do_splice_direct; with 60 sendfile calls, splice_direct = 120, each exactly 64 MiB. One copy fires two hooks, so the product needs the one-layer rule (outermost hook emits, nested splice suppressed).

exec-storm reached only 77 execs/s on the VM (dev container: 633/s with a lighter probe). Cause not separated (VirtualBox-on-Hyper-V process creation vs probe cost). Needs P12 untraced baseline and the Hyper-V on/off experiment before any exec rate is quoted.

Design gap: no record class for file metadata operations (unlink, rename, chmod/chown, link/symlink, mkdir/rmdir, truncate), which carry core attack steps (rename into /usr/bin, chmod +x then exec, deleting evidence). Census v1 also omits connect/accept/bind and the capability family. Census v2 and ADR-0010 must add a META family and these.

Census v2: META (unlink, rmdir, mkdir, rename, link, symlink, chmod, chown, truncate), NET intent (connect, connect_fail, accept, bind, listen) and capability (mmap_shared_w, mprotect_exec, memfd, ptrace, process_vm_writev, io_uring_setup, module_load) classes; hooks and signatures checked in Linux v7.0 source (vfs_mkdir returns struct dentry * in 7.0). Added known-ops self-check workload (census count >= userspace successes) and an attach pre-flight (BTF + ftrace + tracefs). Container dry run: with a probe lacking the hooks, all 20 classes reported MISSED and the run FAILED, as designed. 62 tests; 8/8 mutants killed.

Census v2 on the VM: all 20 new hooks deliver on kernel 7.0 (known-ops: census >= expected for every class, 12 exact). Pre-flight found all 27 functions in BTF+ftrace and 9 tracepoints. file-churn unlinks exact: 68,878 = 68,425 deletes + 449 cleanup + 4 background.

The probe set changes workload speed: with the v2 probe (+20 fexit hooks) syscall rates were 0.17x (super-producer) to 0.70x (xfer) of the v1 run 29 min earlier, and file-churn did 3.6x less work; selectivity was unchanged (exec 0.193/0.193, super-producer 0.067/0.067). Census rates are lower bounds; sizing must use untraced syscall rate x census selectivity. Which hook adds the per-syscall cost is OPEN: A/B bisection next.
exec-storm under v2: mmap_exec ~212/s vs 26 execs/s, about 8 executable library mappings per exec. Emitting code-mapping records would multiply exec-related volume ~8x (input for ADR-0010).

Corrects E-0033: interleaved A/B on fixed work (find /usr x3 serial, 2 rounds) took 2.57 s untraced, 3.28 s under the v1 probe and 2.89 s under v2: v2 is not slower than v1, and tracing costs ~10-35 % here. The 0.17x-0.70x rate drop between the two census runs is not explained by the v2 hooks. Remaining candidates: host drift (runs 29 min apart under Hyper-V) and a concurrency effect (super-producer runs 5 finds in parallel). Selectivity result and the sizing method (untraced rate x selectivity) stand.

Parallel A/B (5 concurrent find /usr, 3 interleaved rounds): untraced 1.59 s, v1 1.85 s (+17 %), v2 2.06 s (+30 %). Contention does not multiply probe cost; v2 costs modestly more than v1 under parallel load. With E-0035, neither the v2 hooks nor concurrency explains the 0.17-0.70x rate drop between census runs; host drift under Hyper-V is the remaining explanation (INF by elimination). Method consequence: absolute rates need interleaved, repeated runs; single census runs are reliable for selectivity and class mix only.

Fixed-work baseline tool (bench/baseline/): find serial/parallel, 2,000 execs, 10 s churn, 20 s fio; untraced vs probe, counterbalanced order, mean/sd/CV per config, slowdown, CV > 10 % flagged not quotable. Container dry run: churn CV 82 % between 2 rounds (the flag fires), disk SKIPPED without fio. 15 tests; mutation 6/6 after strengthening one test.

Hyper-V A-B-A fixed-work baselines (3 rounds each, untraced vs census v2 probe): 2,000 execs untraced took 37.8 s (on, A1), 6.9 s (off, B), 28.1 s (on, A2), i.e. 53 / 292 / 71 execs/s, CV <= 7.4 %. The Windows hypervisor makes process creation 4-5.5x slower; disk 73 / 154 / 119 MB/s. Explains E-0029. Exec tracing slowdown +1 % / +11 % / +8 % (quotable).

Baseline tool defect: jobs contaminated each other through the page cache (untraced find-parallel 0.25-0.27 s in round 1 vs 0.72-0.99 s after churn; find-serial 17.6 s in round 1 after a fresh boot). find/churn means and their slowdowns from A1/B/A2 are not quotable. Fixed: untimed warm-up of each job, same configuration, right before the timed run.

Drift with no configuration change: A1 and A2 (both Hyper-V on) differ by -26 % on exec and +63 % on disk (A1 VM up for hours, A2 fresh boot). On this laptop relative measurements (overhead %, selectivity) are reliable; absolute rates are not. Sizing must use same-session untraced rates; ADR-0012 must fix the authoritative host state.

Windows 11: bcdedit hypervisorlaunchtype off is not enough while Memory integrity (HVCI) is on; VBS status stays 2 and HypervisorPresent stays True. Both must be turned off, and both restored afterwards (verified True / 2 / Enabled 1 / Auto). Runbook section 6a.

Maintainer decision: measurements are taken with the laptop in its everyday safe state (Hyper-V on, Memory integrity on). Only relative results are quoted from it (overhead %, selectivity, loss, class mix, all interleaved within one session); absolute rates are not quoted from this host. Absolute numbers, if needed, come later from better hardware. Goes into ADR-0012.

Warm-up re-run (Hyper-V on, 3 rounds, census v2 probe): the warm-up fix works for its defect (after a fresh boot the cold find-serial, 13.82 s, landed in the untimed warm-up; timed 0.31 s). But all 10 rows have CV 11.8-28.7 %, so no mean is quotable. The noise is fast: back-to-back untraced exec runs took 7.80 s and 12.80 s, 13 s apart; churn 19,990-39,417 ops/s; disk 72.9-171.5 MB/s. Three rounds gated on CV cannot resolve effects of a few percent on this host.

Corrects E-0038: the A-B-A runs did not show that the hypervisor causes the slow exec. With Hyper-V on, as in A1/A2 (operator note), untraced exec took 10.1-12.8 s (warm-ups 7.8-11.7 s) against 37.8 s (A1) and 28.1 s (A2): same-state runs differ by up to 3.3x, close to the 4-5.5x on/off ratio E-0038 attributed to Hyper-V. Something else that changes between boots was not controlled. B (off, 6.9 s) is still the fastest run; E-0042 (relative numbers only) is unaffected.

Census v2 probe and find: traced slower in all 3 timed pairs of both find jobs (paired ratios 1.19-2.79) and in every warm-up pair not hit by the cold cache; magnitude not quotable (OPEN). Likely mechanism (INF on 7.0): the census attaches raw_syscalls sys_enter/exit, so every syscall leaves the fast path (v3.5 on kernel 5.4: about 16 ns per syscall plus per-event cost). exec and churn: ratios on both sides of 1. disk: traced faster in 3 of 3 rounds (0.82-0.85), p = 0.25 by sign test, not interpreted. The census probe is not the product probe; product overhead is measured on the Phase-1 probe.

Maintainer decision: the overhead protocol changes to per-round paired ratios (traced and untraced back to back; median and range) plus an A/A control arm (a second untraced run each round) that measures the run's own noise floor, with at least 7 rounds; an effect is claimed only above that floor. CV stays as a drift indicator, not a quotability gate. Goes into ADR-0012.

Maintainer decision: census-probe overhead is no longer measured. It hooks every syscall through raw_syscalls, which the product does not (E-0045). The next overhead number comes from the Phase-1 probe.
Maintainer decision: install gcc-multilib on the VM, after a snapshot, so that P8's true 32-bit variant runs. It is dev-only and leaves the held kernel untouched.
